name: Big Foot
host_facility: Extended tension-leg drilling and production platform
summary: A dry-tree tension-leg development with reported first oil in November 2018.
narrative: The reported arrangement combines drilling, workover and production on an extended tension-leg platform. Dry trees and top-tensioned risers provide direct well access from the facility. This is a description of the reported selection, not a fresh comparison of host concepts.
architecture: Dry-tree wellheads on the platform connect through top-tensioned risers; processed fluids leave through export infrastructure. No subsea wet-tree layout is implied.
limitations: The source gives inconsistent water-depth figures, so metric water depth is unknown here. Initial producer and injector plans are not an installed-well inventory; well count remains null. Obtain a dated well inventory and facility design basis before drawing a detailed layout or evaluating costs.

name: Anchor
summary: The sanction-date concept is a subsea development served by a semisubmersible production unit.
narrative: The sanction report describes subsea wells feeding a floating production unit in the Lower Tertiary Wilcox trend. This separates seafloor completions from surface processing; the cited selection does not by itself establish equipment qualification or installation feasibility.
architecture: The sanctioned subsea wells connect to a semisubmersible floating production unit. Detailed tree ratings, manifold arrangement and riser geometry require the design basis.
limitations: This page records the 2019 sanction snapshot, not a current well inventory. The lifecycle Explorer reports first oil in August 2024; the cited sanction report only forecasts startup, so it cannot substantiate an actual first-oil year here. A startup source is required before replacing null. The published metric depth and lifecycle block-level estimate remain unresolved, so depth also stays null. Resource lower bounds are not exact reserve estimates. Obtain qualified equipment data before detailed assessment.

name: Jack/St. Malo
summary: Two fields share a semisubmersible host through subsea completions; the source reports startup in December 2014.
narrative: The co-development places the floating production unit between the fields and routes subsea production to a shared processing facility. The source also describes seafloor boosting. Shared-host capacity is not allocated to either field here.
architecture: Jack and St. Malo subsea completions feed the shared floating production unit. The source does not establish a complete well and manifold inventory or measured connection lengths.
limitations: The published host capacity is distinct from the development-stage ramp-up rate. No current capacity allocation, well inventory, water depth or scope-matched reserves are inferred. Obtain those inputs and a dated operating basis before ranking alternatives or evaluating economics.

name: Kaskida
summary: The initial sanctioned phase uses subsea wells and a semisubmersible production host.
narrative: The reported development depended on commercial availability of high-pressure production technology. The initial scope pairs subsea wells with a semisubmersible and preserves expansion as a future decision. No pressure qualification is inferred from the announcement.
architecture: Initial-phase subsea wells feed a semisubmersible production facility. Later-phase wells are outside the well count recorded here.
limitations: The source gives water depth in feet; no conversion is introduced. Startup is a forecast rather than first oil. Obtain an updated schedule, well inventory, metric depth and qualified equipment requirements before evaluating layout, delivery or costs.

name: North Platte
summary: North Platte is represented by the subsequently sanctioned Sparta concept, with subsea wells feeding a semisubmersible host.
narrative: The partner announcement describes a standardized floating production design following earlier host designs, with all-electric compression. Subsea wells connect to the new host. The design rationale is reported from the announcement rather than established by a new optimization.
architecture: The reported development has eight subsea production wells tied back to the Sparta semisubmersible. Well positions, manifold counts and tieback lengths are not supplied.
limitations: The source is a sanction-date snapshot and its startup date is a forecast. Capacity is a design target, not observed production. Resources are reported as exceeding a value, so no exact reserve number is entered. Obtain detailed layout and current scope before quantitative assessment. The published metric depth conflicts with the lifecycle depth, so the concept depth remains unknown. Designed capacity is distinct from the legacy expected-peak statement; its basis requires a separately dated source.

name: Shenandoah
summary: The startup report describes initial-phase subsea production flowing to a floating production system.
narrative: The initial development uses high-pressure subsea technology with production routed to a floating processing system. Later-phase producers and the nearby southern discovery are separate scopes. The startup oil-deliverability target is distinct from host nameplate capacity.
architecture: Initial-phase subsea producers feed the floating production system. The semisubmersible classification follows the committed lifecycle research; the opened startup report calls the host an FPS. Additional-phase and southern-discovery tiebacks are excluded from the recorded well count.
limitations: The initial-phase well count is not the complete later development inventory. The article gives water depth in feet and does not establish metric depth or the full detailed layout. Confirm host classification against its design basis and obtain current phase-specific scope before detailed assessment.

name: Tiber
summary: Tiber is part of the sanctioned Tiber-Guadalupe shared-host development; hub totals are not assigned to Tiber alone.
narrative: The announcement describes a new production hub with Tiber wells and a Guadalupe tieback, reusing Kaskida platform and subsea designs. Design reuse is the reported rationale for delivery efficiencies; no independent cost saving or feasibility calculation is made here.
architecture: Tiber wells and the separate Guadalupe tieback feed one floating production platform. The semisubmersible classification follows the committed lifecycle research; the opened announcement establishes a floating platform and reuse of the Kaskida design, not a detailed hull specification.
limitations: The reported oil capacity and resource totals cover the combined hub. Only the Tiber well count is mapped to FieldConcept; hub resources and forecast startup remain null in Tiber field inputs. Obtain the host design basis, metric depth and scope-specific production allocation before detailed assessment.
